items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: And both Mike and I did solo records too. I would say his were far more successful than mine, but never — when we got together that was always a more special thing. We could never overcome the Brecker Brothers either name or just the image

ctx.x: With everybody being a first call musician on their axes, is that partly why bands break up?

Well you know we never had that problem but from what I understand if there’s big money involved I think that’s why bands somehow break up, from what I’ve heard from other sources and scenes, although I’ve never really been through that myself. But you hear, once again, stories through the grapevine that money can easily get in the way and people think they’re being cheated and they’re not getting paid as much as the next guy. But you know if they’re great players everyone wants to have his say musically I think,…

Great. Thank you. We don’t have to spend a lot of time on this but can you describe what a typical studio session entailed? How do you get the phone call? How much do you know before you get there? And that kind of thing.
